previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with suprapubic and groin pain, burning at the catheter site, and malaise, concerning for recurrent urinary tract infection. He has a chronic indwelling Foley catheter due to hypotonic bladder and a history of multidrug-resistant UTIs. Urinalysis showed infection, and he was started on empiric IV antibiotics. Urine culture grew Acinetobacter baumannii and Enterobacter cloacae, both sensitive to ciprofloxacin. He transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin and completed a catheter change during treatment. His mental confusion on admission resolved quickly and was attributed to sundowning rather than infection. A chest X-ray showed a worsening left pleural effusion but no pneumonia, consistent with his chronic asbestosis. He was discharged to a rehab facility to complete a 14-day course of ciprofloxacin, with plans to follow up with urology and infectious disease for recurrent UTI prevention. His chronic conditions, including CAD, diabetes, hypertension, and a monitored renal mass, remained stable.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ male with history of recent fall with facial abrasion.

COMPARISON:  Non-contrast head CT from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  ___ axial images of the brain were obtained without
intravenous contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformations were prepared.

NON-CONTRAST HEAD CT:  There is no hemorrhage, mass, mass effect, or acute
large territorial infarction.  Mild proportionate enlargement of the
ventricles and sulci are consistent with age-related cortical atrophy.  There
is no shift of the normally-midline structures.  Suprasellar and basilar
cisterns are patent.  Subcentimeter hypodense foci in the basal ganglia and
thalami, bilaterally, are unchanged and likely represent prior lacunar
infarcts.  A 0.8 x 1.6 cm calcific dural-based lesion in the left lateral
aspect of the posterior fossa is unchanged from prior and consistent with a
calcified meningioma. There is extensive atherosclerotic calcification of the
carotid siphons. There is no scalp hematoma or acute skull fracture.  A
mucus-retention cyst is identified within the right sphenoid air cell.  The
remainder of the visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are
well-aerated.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intracranial process.

HISTORY:  ___ male with hypoxia.

COMPARISON:  AP and lateral chest radiograph from ___ and from
___.

SUPINE FRONTAL CHEST RADIOGRAPH:  Patient is rotated and supine, preventing
strict comparison to prior studies. Opacification of the left lung base
appears similar compared to multiple prior examinations and likely reflects a
combination of moderate pleural effusion and associated atelectasis, but
perhaps new consolidation and/or increase in left pleural effusion.  Linear
opacity in the right lung base is suggestive of subsegmental atelectasis. 
Prominent interstitial markings are likely secondary to AP supine technique
and bronchovascular crowding due to low lung volumes.  No overt pulmonary
edema is identified.  Mediastinal and hilar contours appear within normal
limits.  Evaluation of the cardiac silhouette is limited due to basilar
opacities.  No pneumothorax is evident.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Persistent left basilar atelectasis and pleural effusion, new pneumonia
and/or increase in pleural effusion may well be present. Conventional
radiographs recommended, when feasible.
2.  Probable subsegmental atelectasis in the right lung base.
3.  No overt pulmonary edema.
